# 3 Maccabees Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** The Elephants Miraculously Restrained

---

**1** Now Hermon had prepared the aforementioned beasts and was ready to bring them forward at dawn to the hippodrome.

**2** But the Lord sent upon the king a sleep that was deep and pleasant, and thus the Lord foiled his lawless purpose and greatly frustrated his stubborn will.

**3** The king remained there sleeping soundly until late morning; and when he finally woke, released from his heavy sleep, he remembered nothing at all.

**4** He asked the servants around him what had caused him to sleep so late, since it had always been his custom to attend to affairs of state from early morning.

**5** When they explained what had happened, he gave orders that the Jews be brought without delay, and made no mention at all of the elephants.

**6** But when the court officials and above all the Friends of the king heard of this, they were amazed that such a deep sleep had come upon the king, and they praised God for having delivered the Jews.

**7** The Jews, on hearing of the king's change of plans, praised their guardian God and again prayed for his protection, while the bolder among them were greatly encouraged.

**8** Meanwhile Hermon, utterly astonished at the sudden change, went to inform the king, saying: My Lord the King, we are ready to carry out what you commanded, and we await your order to proceed.

**9** But the king looked at him with a terrible expression and said: If your own parents or children had been present, I would have given them to the beasts instead of these Jews, in return for those who have sought to dishonor and betray me.

**10** Hermon, having received this unexpected and dangerous rebuke, was greatly distressed and deeply troubled.

**11** The Friends then gradually turned the king's attention to other matters, and so succeeded in diverting his anger.

**12** Again the same deep and persistent sleep came over the king.

**13** And once again the Jews escaped complete destruction.

**14** After the king had come to himself again, still troubled in his mind, he said: Why have you disturbed me? I gave no such orders regarding these matters.

**15** But when the Friends, the chief stewards and managers of affairs, reminded him, he flew into a sudden rage and gave orders that the Jews be brought to the hippodrome the following morning.

**16** Those who were in charge of the prisoners went away in great confusion and disorder; and returning to the hippodrome they were overcome with pity at the state of the imprisoned Jews.

**17** Among them was Hermon, who was responsible for the whole ordeal, and he mixed wine with frankincense and got the five hundred elephants thoroughly drunk, then drove them forward as the king had commanded.

**18** But a man named Eleazar, prominent among the Jewish priests, called out to the Lord with a loud voice and prayed:

**19** O great King, Most High God, Almighty, who governs all creation with mercy, look upon the descendants of Abraham, upon the children of the sanctified Jacob, upon your holy inheritance, O Father, who are being unjustly put to death as foreigners in a foreign land.

**20** You drove out Egypt and Pharaoh with a hail of plagues when they arrogantly oppressed our holy fathers.

**21** You are the Lord of lords, who governs all creation; look upon us.

**22** Have mercy on us in our bitter distress, and let your mercy save us from this present evil.

**23** Hear our prayer and turn aside the evil being done against us unjustly.

**24** Shatter what is accomplished by the power of arrogance; let him who saved Abraham from the furnace of the Chaldeans also save us.

**25** As you showed mercy to Daniel in the den of lions, and to the three holy youths Ananias, Azariah, and Mishael, so show mercy to us also.
